implementation_notes: Swift makes creation failure a language feature: init?(...) can return nil and init(...) throws can refuse to create an invalid instance, so the type itself carries the factory contract and the classic factory class is not needed; a static factory (make from raw:) is used when the creation path's name must express a domain path. For rebuilding from raw data the stdlib supplies Decodable with init(from: Decoder), which is declared non-failable and throwing - a failable init? cannot satisfy it - so custom decoding must validate and throw (typically DecodingError.dataCorrupted) rather than return nil. Keep the wire shape in a separate RawOrder DTO and let the domain type's initializer own the conversion.
pitfalls: A failable init? cannot satisfy Decodable's non-failable, throwing init(from:) requirement; reconstitution must throw.
A throwing initializer that validates before assigning all stored properties must handle partial initialization; validate a raw DTO first, then assign, to keep the failure path simple.
try? at call sites turns validation failures into nil and erases the reason; propagate the error instead.

variants.name: Decodable init(from:) for reconstitution
variants.implementation_notes: Rebuilding from an external representation is the stdlib's Decodable protocol: implement init(from:) with a private RawOrder DTO and throw a DecodingError when the payload violates a domain rule, so persistence and transport layers get one validated reconstruction path. Choose it when raw data is decoded with JSONDecoder/PropertyListDecoder; keep creation-from-scratch on the throwing initializer, because creation and reconstitution rules differ.
pitfalls: Synthesized Codable conformance writes stored properties directly and bypasses the initializer's validation; synthesize only on raw DTOs and route domain types through a custom init(from:).
Keyed containers throw DecodingError.keyNotFound for missing keys - map those to domain errors deliberately, or callers will report transport failures for domain violations.
Decoders are context-free; invariants that need other aggregates or services cannot be checked during decode, so decode to raw data and run the factory afterwards.
